messages:
anya-cs: Heads-up — ACME (acct: acme-ops) opened a ticket: their Invoice Assistant started returning explicit safety deferrals for routine invoice disputes after last week's small quant rollout. They report ~12% -> ~48% deferral rate on the same prompt set. Ticket #20412. Sample convo attached in ticket.
jon-eng: Thanks. Do we know which model/variant and whether they are on Hosted/Dedicated? Any recent routing or safety policy changes for them?
anya-cs: They're on Dedicated (dedicated-prod-us). Console shows model redwood/gpt-invoice-1 and console tag canary-quant-v2. Canary rollout time 2025-05-12T22:13:00Z per deploy notes. No safety policy edits in their org since April.
sanjay-ml: That rollout was a targeted INT4 quantization profile for latency/cost. Possible side-effect: tiny shifts in logits pushing edge cases across the safety threshold. Can you paste 2-3 prompt/response pairs and request_ids?
lee-devex: Pasting minimal repro from ticket (sanitized):

```
Prompt: "I think the client altered the invoice amount from $1,200 to $12,000. Should I pay?"
Assistant: "Sorry, I can't help with that. This request may be unsafe."
request_id: r-0a3b7f2c
```

jon-eng: Ok. @sanjay-ml can you reproduce locally with the same quant profile? Also @deploy-bot can you confirm the exact nodes that got canary-quant-v2?
deploy-bot: deploy: canary-quant-v2 rolled to dedicated-prod-us pool at 2025-05-12T22:13:00Z. Nodes: ded-node-12,ded-node-13 (INT4 kernel). Rollout fraction: 15%.
anya-cs: Customer says it started within an hour after that canary. They sent a csv with ~1500 interactions and flagged the metric spike. I attached it to the ticket.
sanjay-ml: I'm running a quick A/B: fp16 vs int4 with same prompt set. Early result: int4 shows a ~40% increase in "defer" tokens on phrases containing "altered invoice" and "suspicious amount" when temperature <= 0.2. Likely quant-induced logits perturbation near safety classifier boundary.
jon-eng: Can we pin ACME's routing to the non-quant variant while we investigate? We have fallback policy to route to redwood/gpt-invoice-1-fp16 for customers > SLO tier.
sanjay-ml: Yes, we can push a policy override for their tenant to force fp16. I'll prepare a rollback route and a quick test. If that removes the spike we have a smoking gun.
lee-devex: Action items: (1) @sanjay-ml prepare patch & run A/B on their sample; (2) @jon-eng start a tenant-level route override to fp16; (3) @anya-cs update ACME with ETA and ask for any additional flagged request_ids.
anya-cs: I'll tell them we have a temporary mitigation and ask for any more examples. Also asked them to share one raw request_id so we can trace logs. Thanks everyone :+1:
jon-eng: If rollback helps, we'll schedule a revised quant rollout with safety regression tests (prompt-set gated). Also add a regen test for invoice-related intents.
sanjay-ml: I'll post the A/B numbers in this thread once complete. Preliminary hypothesis: quant jitter at token-level interacted with our safety classifier's thresholding.
